JavaScript stops after adding the food because its hold_another_object call has no encumberMessage callback; C continues through invent.c:hold_another_object to pickup.c:encumber_msg. source.branch: For a charged, applied horn of plenty with tipping false, hornoplenty consumes a charge, creates food, prints its spill message, and passes the generated object to invent.c:hold_another_object. Once the object remains in inventory, that function calls pickup.c:encumber_msg before returning to hornoplenty.
callers: apply.c:doapply(HORN_OF_PLENTY) -> mkobj.c:hornoplenty; js/apply.js:doapply calls js/obj.js:hornoplenty with only {state}.
mkobj.c:hornoplenty -> invent.c:hold_another_object; js/obj.js:hornoplenty forwards the unaugmented env to js/invent.js:hold_another_object.
dependencies: invent.c:hold_another_object is implemented in js/invent.js but currently demands hooks.encumberMessage at its successful-inventory tail; the source calls the linked pickup.c function directly.

pickup.c:encumber_msg is implemented and already imported in js/obj.js. Wire the C callback generally for hornoplenty’s non-tipping path and preserve the complete source branch, including the generated-object return and PRNG order.
